images.title: Onion prices of two towns on one dot plot
images.purpose: Show all 24 monthly onion prices of Yahapur and Wahapur as dots on one number line so their spread can be compared.
images.composition: One long horizontal number line across the frame with two rows of dots above it, a legend at the top right.
exact_structure: A horizontal number line from 10 to 60 with a tick at every whole number and a numbered tick at 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 and 60, drawn in dark grey (#2B2B2B).
Exactly 12 green (#009E73) dots for Yahapur, one dot above each of these values: 24, 25, 26, 28, 30, 35, 39, 43, 44, 49, 56, 59.
Exactly 12 purple (#CC79A7) dots for Wahapur, one dot above each of these values: 17, 19, 23, 30, 35, 38, 39, 42, 42, 52, 53, 60.
Where two or more dots fall on the same value they are stacked one above another, never overlapping; the value 30 carries one green and one purple dot, 35 carries one green and one purple dot.
A legend in the top right corner: a green dot labelled Yahapur and a purple dot labelled Wahapur.
An axis caption below the line reads Price of onions (in rupees per kg).
labels: Price of onions (in rupees per kg)
rejection: dots not stacked where values repeat
month names written on the dots
a total other than 12 dots per town
images.takeaway: Wahapur's prices are spread wider (17 to 60) than Yahapur's (24 to 59), though both crowd the middle twenties to forties.
images.description: A dot plot with 12 green dots for Yahapur and 12 purple dots for Wahapur on a line from 10 to 60.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Ask which town has the lowest and highest dot, and what the dot plot hides (the months).

image_decisions.why: The dot plot is the mathematics of this concept; students must see both towns' dots on one line.
